column1: # The settings a user can change, one per line, its fields separated by tabs:
# name (its environment variable), kind (seconds, count:<least>, share, flag,
# choice:<a,b,c>, word, mutators), default (empty when it is worked out),
# who may set it (project: a project's .sheriff.properties too; project:<image>:
# a project's file too, but only to that image, a tag or a digest of it; user:
# only the user's own file), and what it does, as sheriff_config and the user's
# file say. A line "## Title" starts a section, which the settings page shows

column5: Sheriff's image. A digest, kaizten/sheriff@sha256:..., keeps one build, as Sheriff is published only as latest. A project's file may set only kaizten/sheriff; another image, only your own file.
always pulls a newer image when the server starts, check only says one is published, never does not ask.
The rule profile, over the project's declaration, for the components written in its language. Empty: the declared one, else the one the sources call for.
Seconds one run of Sheriff gets (900 through WSL's Docker).
Rounds of Sheriff's own fixers in a repair, each measured by a new analysis. Empty: until a round repairs nothing.
1 makes the hooks stop Sheriff at the first error.
Seconds the hooks reuse a verdict before running Sheriff again.
Times in a row the Stop hook sends a turn back while errors remain.
Stops in a row with nothing changed that the Stop hook still sends back. 0 lets the first through, as a false positive needs.

column1: ## Tests, and how well they test the change

column5: 1 is for trying an idea out: a component is done when Sheriff finds no errors, with no tests asked for, run or measured, by the tools, the Stop hook or the repair loop. Set it back to 0 before the work is kept.
1 makes the Stop hook require green tests, and measure how well they test the turn's change.
Seconds the project's tests get when the MCP tools run them (sheriff_fix with verify); VERIFICATION_TIMEOUT is the hooks' and the repair loop's.
Seconds the project's tests get in the hooks and the repair loop (sheriff_autofix); SHERIFF_TEST_TIMEOUT is the MCP tools'.
Share of the lines a change wrote that its tests must run. A pom.xml's sheriff.coverage, or coverage in a project's .sheriff.properties, wins over the files.
Share of the branches of those lines' conditions its tests must take. A pom.xml's sheriff.branches, or branches in a project's .sheriff.properties, wins over the files.
Share of PIT's mutants of those lines its tests must kill. A pom.xml's sheriff.mutation, or mutation in a project's .sheriff.properties, wins over the files.
PIT's mutators, or groups (DEFAULTS, STRONGER, ALL). A pom.xml's sheriff.mutators, or mutators in a project's .sheriff.properties, wins over the files.
Seconds the tests get under JaCoCo.
Seconds PIT gets.
Passes of the repair loop. Empty: sized from the errors, and grown while they drop.
Files the repair loop gives a model at once.
Rules of a profile the repair loop puts in one prompt. Empty: the loop's own limit.
1 makes the repair loop work on a branch of its own, commit each pass and stop when a model edits a file outside its batch; 0 edits the working tree as it is, with none of that.
Who answers in the repair loop.
Seconds one pass of claude gets in the repair loop (AI_BACKEND=claude_cli).
The command that runs codex in the repair loop, without the prompt (AI_BACKEND=codex_cli).
Seconds one pass of codex gets in the repair loop (AI_BACKEND=codex_cli).
The command that runs agy in the repair loop, without the prompt; --model claude-sonnet-5-5-high, from agy models, picks the model (AI_BACKEND=antigravity_cli).
Seconds one pass of agy gets in the repair loop (AI_BACKEND=antigravity_cli).

column1: ## The API backends of the repair loop

column5: The model anthropic_api asks. Its key is read only from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, never from a file.
Where anthropic_api sends its requests. Empty: Anthropic's own API.
The most tokens one answer of anthropic_api may take.
Times one pass of anthropic_api may read or write a file before it is cut.
The model openai_api or local asks. Empty: gpt-4o-mini for openai_api, qwen2.5-coder for local. Its key is read only from OPENAI_API_KEY, never from a file.
Where openai_api or local sends its requests, such as an LM Studio or vLLM server. Empty: https://api.openai.com/v1 for openai_api, Ollama's http://localhost:11434/v1 for local.
The most tokens one answer of openai_api or local may take; a model that thinks before answering needs more.
Times one pass of openai_api or local may read or write a file before it is cut.
